verdict.rationale: The evidence pack never mentions blocking senders' tracking pixels or remote images, so the core protection part of the story is unevidenced. The data-transparency part is thinly covered. The README states Zero does not track, collect, or sell user data, and it discloses that emails are stored in a Durable Object and an R2 bucket. missing for 10: default read-pixel/remote-image blocking, any sender-tracking protection controls, a detailed privacy policy or data-handling documentation, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a switcher, the client protects me from senders' tracking — blocking read pixels by default — and is transparent about what it does with my mail data

citations.quote: Your emails, your data. Zero does not track, collect, or sell your data in any way.
We're now storing the user's emails in their Durable Object & an R2 bucket.
